messages.author: 7f7355d1143e7e9f
messages.subject: An endless spatio-temporal modelling
parts:
Dear all,
I would like to predict the spatio-temporal schistosomiasis risk in my study area using sample village-level data (i.e., No. of infected individuals and No. of population at risk) between 2005-2010. I ran the following coding, but it is always endless. Can someone point out where the problem is? Thank you! 

BTW, I have changed resolution of the mesh, but the procedure is still endless.

mydata<-read.csv("G:/schistosomiasis/guichi/guichi.csv",header=TRUE,sep=",")
head(mydata)

mydata is as follows
  VillageID         CM  POINT_X POINT_Y  R6 R8 year    river
1         1 孔井居委会 543823.2 3390654 981 70 2005  1026.56
2         2 十里居委会 543072.0 3386813 669  0 2005  2212.47
3         3 长岗居委会 543256.7 3388562 638 31 2005  1474.28
4         6     低岭村 572830.9 3391545 973 15 2005 15680.83
5         7     河口村 571306.7 3390207 829  8 2005 16375.35
6         9     龙池村 565170.0 3383849 866 10 2005 20806.61
the projection coordinate information (CRS("+proj=utm +zone=50 +datum=WGS84") 

guichi.mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(loc.domain=border, max.edge=c(5000, 10000))
plot(guichi.mesh)

#############estimate 
mydata$time<-rep(1:7,each=41)
guichi.spde<-inla.spde2.matern(mesh=guichi.mesh,alpha=2)

A.est <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh=guichi.mesh,loc=cbind(mydata$POINT_X,mydata$POINT_Y),
group=mydata$time,n.group=7)

s.index <- inla.spde.make.index(name="spatial.field",
n.spde=guichi.spde$n.spde, n.group=7)

stack.est <- inla.stack(data=list(y=mydata$R8,n=mydata$R6),
A=list(A.est, 1), effects=list(c(s.index,list(Intercept=1)),
list(river=mydata[,8]/1000)), tag="est")    

####predicted locations within border were selected
guichi.pred<- readOGR("G:/schistosomiasis/guichi","pred_all")
river.pred<-guichi.pred$NEAR_DIST

A.pred <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh=guichi.mesh,
loc=coordinates(guichi.pred),
group=1, #selected day for prediction
n.group=7)

stack.pred <- inla.stack(data=list(y=NA,n=1),
A=list(A.pred,1),
effects=list(c(s.index,list(Intercept=1)),
list(river=river.pred/1000)),
tag="pred")

stack<-inla.stack(stack.est,stack.pred)

formu<- y~ -1+Intercept+river+f(spatial.field, model=guichi.spde, 
group=spatial.field.group, control.group=list(model="ar1"))

output<-inla(formu, data=inla.stack.data(stack,spde=guichi.spde),
family="zeroinflated.binomial.1",Ntrials=n,
control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stack),compute=T))

In the end, the interface of R is as follows but the programming was still running

  inla.stack.index(stack, tag="pred")$data
gives the indices into fitted.values corresponding to the predictor you specified in a stack with tag "pred".
